implementation_architecture.step: 1. Cooperative signal scope and acquired child
implementation_architecture.instruction: Before Popen, install temporary SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers that only record interruption in a fixed-size state (for example first signal and a boolean); they must not raise, exit, perform cleanup, append an unbounded log, or do I/O. Keep them active through bounded_run finalization, then restore previous handlers in guarded teardown. Restore a partially installed handler set if installation fails, before any spawn. Do not block these signals across Popen: that would pass blocked signals to the child. Thus a cooperative signal at the Popen return/assignment boundary records intent without discarding the returned proc. Immediately acquire phase=owned before fallible bookkeeping. On exception, a non-null proc in pre-owned/not-spawned phase is still acquired ownership unless a reap transition has begun; never call that successful no-child cleanup. At the first safe checkpoint after acquisition, and inside the existing bounded collection/wait loops, convert a recorded signal into the ordinary primary failure path. Scope the guarantee to these cooperative OS signals and the existing fixed deliberate exceptions; do not invent arbitrary Popen-internal failures or a new supervisor.

Every waitpid enters phase=reap-uncertain before calling the potentially reaping syscall. Only definite waited==0 restores owned; waited==proc.pid sets reaped and stores raw status before any fallible conversion. Unexpected return/exception remains uncertain and permanently forbids group signaling. Only owned/acquired-before-first-reap may call killpg, at most once. Cooperative handlers do not raise inside this transfer. The existing short waitpid mask may remain if correctly restored, but is unnecessary for the non-raising handlers; do not add blocking across spawn. Set proc.returncode from known raw status on both normal and cleanup reap paths, guarded so conversion failure never restores signal permission. No poll, wait, communicate or hidden second reap path.

Replace return-inside-try plus duplicate selector closes with one finalizer that runs before returning a result or raising the recorded failure. Retain bounded output material and the first failure separately. Normal streaming may close a pipe at EOF or after stdin completion, using the same small close bookkeeping used by finalization; do not close it a second time. Record a successful close/already-observed closed state per stdin/stdout/stderr, and absent/closed/failed for the selector. Selector.close is called only once, in guarded finalization. For each remaining pipe, draining and closing are separate guarded operations so a failed set_blocking/read cannot skip the close. Guard each independent cleanup obligation against BaseException, record its error, and continue the other obligations. An attempted failed close is failed/uncertain, not closed; do not retry it through an unguarded finally or infer closure from reaching finally. A small local closure helper is fine; do not build a resource framework.

For an owned failure, establish the existing one shared two-second cleanup deadline, attempt the single permitted SIGKILL, nonblockingly drain/discard stdout/stderr, close all pipes and selector independently, and reap with WNOHANG and positive bounded sleeps within that same allowance. With uncertain/reaped phase, never signal; uncertain ownership remains terminal failed. Non-raising signal handlers stay installed throughout all these obligations, including their bookkeeping. Use a separate fixed cleanup_interrupted flag, set by the handler when finalization is active, so a repeated signal during cleanup remains visible even if a signal was already recorded during collection. Continue obligations without resetting the deadline. An actual caught deliberate KeyboardInterrupt is also recorded without skipping later obligations. Mark interrupted or uncertain cleanup failed even when individual resources subsequently close/reap; preserve the primary failure plus cleanup errors separately. No unbounded wait, drain, retry or signal log.

Set aggregate cleanup success only after the finalizer, known leader reap (or no acquired child), all required pipe closes and selector close, and guarded handler restoration have succeeded without cleanup interruption. Keep per-resource outcomes separate from aggregate errors. Finalization error after normal collection becomes a primary failure; finalization error after an earlier failure is appended without replacing that first failure. Never return success before selector finalization. In the single-probe caller, set failure for response/probe-validation errors before writing lifecycle.json; persist through one guarded success/failure completion path when possible. Receipt-write failure remains nonzero. Retain current top-level diagnostic policy for its separate card; lifecycle persistence must not rely on a literal cleanup success field or swallow a failure.

implementation_architecture.step: 6. Minimum source restoration and probe addition
implementation_architecture.instruction: Restore pending stdin to the newline-terminated bytes b'review fixture\n' rather than bytes containing a literal backslash and n. Keep the existing saved remaining-duration sleep calculation as an explicitly accepted inseparable safety improvement; do not reintroduce its negative-sleep race. Preserve all seven existing lifecycle controls. Add only lifecycle-cleanup-interrupt: after acquiring the one real adapter child, raise a fixed setup Failure, and at the first cleanup point send exactly one SIGINT to the harness itself while the deferred handler is active, before cleanup obligations. It must complete bounded cleanup, preserve the setup failure and signal observation, report cleanup failed due to interruption, persist resource/reap outcomes, and exit nonzero. No second signal mode or handoff-fault matrix is necessary; the handoff is primarily a source-proof obligation.

required_behavior: Repair the three review26 findings as one ownership correction. Keep the existing fixed environment PATH=/usr/bin:/bin, private HOME, LANG=C; actual adapter and sibling; validated absolute interpreter; native sandbox-exec and no-network/no-fork/write-only-output sandbox. Retain 4096 stream caps, 16384 record cap, ten-second invocation, 180-second suite and two-second cleanup allowance.

Keep --adapter ABS, --output-dir ABS and the closed scenario enum with matrix default. Reject unknown scenarios before spawn. Every non-matrix lifecycle scenario runs at most one actual adapter invocation. No arbitrary command, expression, timeout, signal, fake program or runner input.

Keep lifecycle observations small and fixed: spawned PID, signal attempt phase and result, reap status, each pipe/selector close status, deferred interruption, first failure and bounded cleanup errors. Cleanup signal bookkeeping must distinguish intended/attempted/failed action; no success inferred from appending an attempt.

Every injected failure and uncertain cleanup is nonzero and stops the suite. Normal lifecycle exits zero only after original response validation and successful actual finalization. No post-reap signal under any normal, fixed-fault or cleanup path.

No claim of resistance to SIGKILL, interpreter crashes, arbitrary monkeypatched operations or an endless signal storm. Existing cooperative SIGINT/SIGTERM and designated faults are the finite contract. Resource I/O remains nonblocking and cleanup deadline remains fixed.
